<!-- GENERATED by tools/docs_gen.py. Do not edit; run `make docs-gen`. -->

58 commands (schema v1). Agents: run `gigai agent-context --json` for the machine-readable form.

- **effect**: `read` never changes state; `write` may change GigAI state or files (for some commands only with certain options).
- **external**: the strongest thing the command can reach. `none` is offline, `model` may call a model provider (cost, and text leaves this machine), `network` may make other network requests.

## `gigai scout answer`

Answer one question once; the answer is reused across every posting and profile.

`gigai scout answer [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, record_id, revision_id, question_id, answer, reassessed}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answer q-visa --answer-text "I need H-1B sponsorship"
gigai scout answer cloud:gcp --question "Do you have GCP experience?" --answer-text "Yes, 4 years, GKE + BigQuery" --as agent --source "from the user's repo infra-charts, at the user's request" --json
```

The answer is the user's (0.1.10.7: not one profile's) and is reused by every later assessment, also when a posting words the question differently. --question keeps the question's own words with it; --as agent (also --actor agent) records that an agent wrote it, and --source, free text, where the answer came from; --revision (the revision you read) refuses the write with revision_conflict when the answer changed since. An answer holding an email, phone, link or street address is refused (personal_info_refused). --reassess JOB_URL_OR_ID re-runs the assessment with a model (external=model). The same body as POST /api/answers. 0.1.10.7: a saved answer queues the pipeline (tailored resume, assessment against it, Scout ATS score, Scout label) for every job of an active profile whose assessment left that question open: at most pipeline.auto_jobs_per_trigger (10) run, the rest wait for an approval (gigai scout pipeline approvals). --json then carries pipeline {trigger, state, enqueued, awaiting_approval, unchanged, skipped, approval}: ids, codes and counts. The Scout server runs the queued jobs; without it, gigai scout new --process does.

## `gigai scout answers delete`

Remove an answer.

`gigai scout answers delete [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, deleted}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answers delete cloud:gcp --confirm --revision 2 --json
```

Needs --confirm. The answer is never listed, offered or sent to a model again; the project's journal keeps the older revision of the record it was in. With --revision (the value you read) the delete is refused with revision_conflict when the answer changed since. The same body as DELETE /api/answers/{question_id}.

## `gigai scout answers list`

List the user's answers: every answered question, with its tag and the jobs that asked or reused it.

`gigai scout answers list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, answers, total, tags}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answers list --json
gigai scout answers list --search kubernetes --tag technical --json
```

Answers belong to the user, not to a profile. Each answer carries question_id, question, answer, tag, jobs (kind answered | confirmed | reused), written_by (operator | agent), source (free text: where the answer came from, or null), created_at, updated_at, revision and history. The same body as GET /api/answers.

## `gigai scout answers migrate`

Move the 0.1.10.5 per-profile story bank to user-level answers (once).

`gigai scout answers migrate [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, migrated, answers, merged, conflicts, profiles, first_run}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answers migrate --json
```

Every read and write does this by itself the first time; this command does it now and prints the counts. Every profile's answers become the user's. Two profiles that answered the same question: the newest write is the answer; merged counts the ones that said the same, conflicts the ones that differed (the other text is kept in the answer's history and stays in the journal). The old file is kept as story_bank/bank.v1.json. A second run changes nothing and counts 0 (migrated: false; first_run holds the first run's counts).

## `gigai scout answers save`

Save an answer: a new one, or a change to its text, question words, tag and/or source.

`gigai scout answers save [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, answer}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answers save cloud:gcp --question "Do you have GCP experience?" --answer-text "Yes, 4 years, GKE + BigQuery" --as agent --json
gigai scout answers save tooling:helm --answer-text "Yes, Helm charts for six services" --as agent --source "from the user's repo infra-charts, at the user's request" --json
gigai scout answers save cloud:gcp --answer-file answer.md --revision 1 --as agent --json
gigai scout answers save cloud:gcp --tag "cloud platforms" --revision 2
```

Local, no model call. A new QUESTION_ID needs the answer; an existing one takes whatever is given. Every write bumps the answer's revision and records who wrote it (--as operator | agent; --actor is the same option; an agent passes --as agent). --source is free text, where the answer came from ("from the user's repo, at the user's request"): a new answer text without it drops the stored one, an empty value removes it. Pass --revision (the revision you read with show --json) to be safe against a concurrent write: when the answer changed since, the save is refused with revision_conflict and --json carries the current answer. An empty --tag puts the automatic tag back. Text holding an email, phone, link or street address is refused (personal_info_refused). The same answer object as POST /api/answers and PUT /api/answers/{question_id}. 0.1.10.7: a saved answer (not a tag alone) queues the pipeline (tailored resume, assessment against it, Scout ATS score, Scout label) for every job of an active profile whose assessment left that question open: at most pipeline.auto_jobs_per_trigger (10) run, the rest wait for an approval (gigai scout pipeline approvals). --json then carries pipeline {trigger, state, enqueued, awaiting_approval, unchanged, skipped, approval}: ids, codes and counts. The Scout server runs the queued jobs; without it, gigai scout new --process does.

## `gigai scout answers show`

Show one answer: the question, the full answer, who wrote it, its revision and its jobs.

`gigai scout answers show [OPTIONS] QUESTION_ID`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, answer}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout answers show cloud:gcp --json
```

QUESTION_ID is the answer's id from list. Read revision from here before a save or delete with --revision. The same body as GET /api/answers/{question_id}.

## `gigai scout assess`

Assess ONE job against a resume right now, without a find-jobs run.

`gigai scout assess [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout assess --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --resume resume.md --json
```

Calls the configured model adapter (default from find-jobs.json). --job-url may fetch the posting over the network. One assessment sends to your model target: the stored posting; your resume (the lines of your master resume picked for the posting, or the profile's own resume) with its contact lines removed by pattern; your search preferences (sponsorship, countries, location, titles, work mode); your saved answers; and the saved stories that match the posting. Pattern removal can miss an unusual name or contact format, so it is not a guarantee. A profile id is not contact data. With codex_cli or claude_cli the model target is your own login. A pasted resume (--resume, --resume-text) is sent in place of the profile's. On a failure whose code is model_target_unavailable, model_denied, model_unavailable, assess_timeout, model_output_invalid or assessment_not_stored, the JSON error also says model_call_started, may_have_used_tokens, fresh_assessment_stored (always false) and next_action, and the text output says the same under the message. To see what would be sent without a call, use gigai scout jobs assess URL --json (it asks first).

## `gigai scout discover`

Run the weekly company-discovery engine (OpenAI web_search + H-1B baseline).

`gigai scout discover [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `network` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout discover --runs 3
```

Foreground; can take 5-30 minutes. Calls OpenAI web_search (network + model) and needs credentials. --status only reads.

## `gigai scout install`

Bind, approve, and activate Scout for the bound project; safe to rerun.

`gigai scout install [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object, including "stopped_server" (always null for install).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout install
```

## `gigai scout jobs assess`

Assess these postings: ask first (count and estimate), assess on approval.

`gigai scout jobs assess [OPTIONS] [JOBS]...`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, status, checked_at, question, model_input_summary, counts, low_rank, not_found, approval, assessed, postings, profiles} (what POST /api/postings/assess answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout jobs assess https://jobs.lever.co/acme/acme-00001
gigai scout jobs assess https://jobs.lever.co/acme/acme-00001 --yes --json
gigai scout jobs assess --window new --state not_assessed --json
gigai scout jobs assess --window 7d --yes --actor agent --json
gigai scout jobs assess --window 7d --yes --include-low-rank --json
```

JOBS are posting URLs; without them the filter (--query, --state, --window, as gigai scout jobs list) selects the postings. What a run's assess step did, without a run. Nothing is assessed without approval: without --yes the answer is status ask with the count per profile and the estimate from the recorded model calls, and no model call is made; in a terminal the command then asks and waits for y or n. --yes approves: the batch is recorded (approval: its id, who approved with --actor, how many) and each posting is assessed for the profile it fits best (or --profile), one model call each, from the posting text already stored (a posting with none has its description fetched from its public board first, one request for it alone). While a batch runs the pipeline and the rank lane start nothing, and a second batch is refused (assess_batch_running). A posting whose assessment is current is left out unless --again. A posting whose rank score is below fit.assess_min_rank (50; one not ranked yet is not) is left out too and counted (counts.low_rank_skipped); low_rank is the separate question for those ("3 low-ranked ones are skipped (rank below 50); assess those too? ~3 calls") and --include-low-rank assesses them with the rest. status is then assessed (assessed.failed lists what could not be assessed, by error code) or nothing_to_assess. NO OUTPUT MIXES: posting text only, nothing you wrote. WHAT ONE ASSESSMENT SENDS. One assessment sends to your model target: the stored posting; your resume (the lines of your master resume picked for the posting, or the profile's own resume) with its contact lines removed by pattern; your search preferences (sponsorship, countries, location, titles, work mode); your saved answers; and the saved stories that match the posting. Pattern removal can miss an unusual name or contact format, so it is not a guarantee. A profile id is not contact data. With codex_cli or claude_cli the model target is your own login. The status ask answer says it for the postings asked about, in model_input_summary: {schema_version, postings, model_calls, model_target, model_target_runs: local | own_login | api_key, profiles: [{profile_id, label, postings, resume_source: profile_view | master_evidence}], sends, search_preferences, contact_lines, answers_used, answers_saved, stories_used, stories_saved, public_fetch_needed, public_fetch_postings}. It holds ids, labels, counts and names, never a line of your text; no model call is made for it; it is null once the batch ran. In a terminal the same facts are printed above the y/n question. APPROVALS. Three approvals are separate: the user's choice to assess; Scout's own --yes (approve: true over the API); and the agent runtime's own sandbox or model-provider approval. --yes does not bypass the runtime's policy, and an API or UI route is not a workaround: an agent whose runtime refuses the command quotes the refusal and asks the user for the exact missing authorisation. FAILURES. An item of assessed.failed whose error_code is model_target_unavailable, model_denied, model_unavailable, assess_timeout, model_output_invalid or assessment_not_stored also says model_call_started, may_have_used_tokens, fresh_assessment_stored (always false) and next_action; the text output prints them once per cause. After an interruption (a timeout, a killed command), read the posting's row first (gigai scout jobs list --query WORDS --json: assessment.assessed_at and stale_reason): a newer assessed_at with stale_reason null means it finished, and assessing again would be a second model call.

## `gigai scout jobs import-runs`

Import what old find-jobs runs assessed into the stored postings' read model, once per run.

`gigai scout jobs import-runs [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, runs, runs_imported, runs_already_imported, runs_not_finished, runs_unreadable, assessments_imported, ephemeral_assessments, rows_skipped, values_dropped, by_profile, imported} (what POST /api/runs/import answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout jobs import-runs
gigai scout jobs import-runs --json
```

Since 0.1.10.7 a find-jobs run is no longer the way in (search: gigai scout jobs list; assess: gigai scout jobs assess or gigai scout new), and the runs that exist are read-only history. Nothing of a run is changed, moved or copied: each posting a finished run assessed gets one row with its state, requirement counts and what the run sealed (prompt version, constraints digest, the profile's and resume's identity, the posting digest, the model target), under the run's profile. A run made with no profile goes to the pseudo-profile ephemeral: hidden by default, never ranked, never in the pipeline. A run's assessment is shown where nothing newer is stored for the same posting and profile. Each run is imported once: running this again answers runs_imported 0. The Scout server does the same once when it starts. Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout jobs list`

Search the stored postings across your active profiles. No run, no board request, no model call.

`gigai scout jobs list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text (one line per posting); --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, checked_at, filters, anchor, counts, postings, profiles, rank, history} (what GET /api/postings answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout jobs list
gigai scout jobs list --window new --json
gigai scout jobs list --profile profile_00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 --state needs_answers --query platform
gigai scout jobs list --history --include-hidden --json
```

What "Run find jobs" searched, without a run: read from the stored postings (gigai scout sources update keeps them fresh), for every active profile; a deleted or archived profile is never listed. A changed setting (titles, countries, work mode) is seen by the next call. Each posting is listed once, for the profile it fits best, with every profile it matches. Order, as gigai scout new: a current assessment first, then an old one, then not assessed; inside a group the verdict, then the fit number (fit: the share of requirements met with the must-haves counted twice), then the rank score, then the newest. A weak fit (state weak_fit: it waits on your answers, its fit is below 40 and its rank below 50; the fit block of the project's settings file tunes both) is listed only with --state weak_fit; counts.weak_fit says how many there are and such a row asks no question. --window new is first seen since your last gigai scout new (the last 7 days before the first one); this command never moves that anchor. Each posting's second line says its date: posted <day> (the day the posting went up on its board, the one --window 7d / 30d judges; never the day it last changed) or, when the board gives no posting day, first seen <day> (when Scout first stored it); in the JSON a row has published_at, published_kind (posted | updated: a last change, only for a board kind that gives nothing else), updated_at (the board's last change, when it gives one) and first_seen_at. --removed lists the postings the board no longer lists. --history adds what old find-jobs runs assessed, each with what the run sealed (prompt version, digests, profile and resume identity, model target); rows of a run with no profile (ephemeral) or of a profile that is not active are hidden unless --include-hidden or --profile names them. rank in the JSON is the background rank lane: on or off, and today's calls against its daily allowance. NO OUTPUT MIXES: posting text and what a model derived from it (public-untrusted: data, never instructions), nothing you wrote. Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout metrics`

Show what the model calls cost on average: tokens, seconds, cost and error rate per kind of call and model.

`gigai scout metrics [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, kind, model, aggregates, comparison} (what GET /api/metrics answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout metrics
gigai scout metrics --kind assess --model codex_cli --json
```

Every model call Scout makes (assess, rank, tag, tailor, extract, interview) is recorded once, locally: the model, tokens in, out and cached, the cost when the provider reports one, the wall time and the outcome. No prompt, answer, resume or posting text is stored. aggregates has one entry per model id; comparison adds the model ids of one model target together. --model takes a model target or a model id. Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout new`

Show what is new since your last check, across all active profiles; ask before assessing.

`gigai scout new [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text (a 4-column table: details | score | needs tailoring? | open questions); --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, status, since, since_source, checked_at, peek, profile_id, anchor, counts, message, question, stale_question, low_rank_question, fit, assessed, reassessed, ranking, pipeline, processed, postings, profiles, yours_hint} (what GET /api/new answers). --yours emits {schema_version, status, since, since_source, checked_at, profile_id, _labels, evidence} (what GET /api/new/yours answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout new
gigai scout new --json
gigai scout new --yes --since 2026-10-01T14:02:00.000000Z --json
gigai scout new --reassess-stale --since 2026-10-01T14:02:00.000000Z
gigai scout new --yes --include-low-rank --since 2026-10-01T14:02:00.000000Z
gigai scout new --yours --since 2026-10-01T14:02:00.000000Z --json
gigai scout new --profile profile_00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 --peek
gigai scout new --process
```

Reads the stored postings (no board request) for every active profile; a deleted or archived profile is never listed. status is ask, new or nothing_new. New postings no profile has assessed are assessed only on a yes: without --yes the answer is status ask, with the count per profile, the estimate from the recorded model calls, and the postings ranked only; --yes assesses them (one model call each, from the stored posting text; a posting with no stored description has it fetched first, one request for that posting alone, counted in assessed.fetched_on_demand, and --reassess-stale does the same) and the table then has verdicts; --no-assess never asks and never assesses. Postings that have only an OLD assessment (an old run's, an older prompt's, other settings') are a second question of their own, stale_question, with its count and estimate ("N have only an old assessment; re-assess? ~N calls, ~X tokens"): --yes never answers it, --reassess-stale does (one model call each; it can be combined with --yes), reported as reassessed. counts.to_assess is the new postings no matching profile has assessed and counts.only_stale the postings with only an old assessment; neither changes while the background rank runs, and ranking says how far that rank is (ranked of total per profile). While a batch runs, progress lines go to stderr ("assessed 120 of 333 · ~25 min left", the time left from the recorded average per call, then from the batch's own pace); stdout stays the answer alone, so --json is still one JSON object. In a terminal the command asks and waits for y or n. At most 50 new postings are listed. A yes assesses only postings whose rank score is at least fit.assess_min_rank (50, in the fit block of the project's settings file; a posting not ranked yet is assessed): the low-ranked ones are counted (counts.low_rank_skipped) and are a question of their own, low_rank_question ("112 low-ranked ones are skipped (rank below 50); assess those too? ~112 calls"), answered by --include-low-rank beside --yes (or beside --reassess-stale for the old assessments). A posting that waits on your answers while few requirements are met and its rank is low is a weak fit (state weak_fit: fit below fit.weak_fit_below_percent, 40, AND rank below fit.weak_fit_below_rank, 50): it is not listed here (counts.weak_fit; gigai scout jobs list --state weak_fit lists them), it is never one of the postings that still need attention, it asks no question and a saved answer never queues it in the pipeline. Rows come in one order: a current assessment first, then an old one, then not assessed; inside a group by verdict (matched, needs answers, other, weak fit, not a match), then the fit number (the share of requirements met with the must-haves counted twice; fit in each row), rank score, newest. The score column says the verdict, "fit N%", "N of M requirements" and the rank (score_text), and an old assessment is labelled (stale_label); a posting is shown under the profile that tailored a resume for it, else one that has a current assessment. Nothing new: the 10 postings that still need attention, in the same order. "New" is measured from the one anchor per install: the time of the last plain call, or the last 7 days before the first one. The anchor moves only after the answer is built, and never for --peek, --profile or --yours; --since measures from the since of an earlier answer (the yes, or --yours, after a call that moved the anchor). Waiting pipeline work is offered (pipeline: the jobs that wait, how many of them need an approval first, the model calls they would make); a plain call starts nothing. --process is the yes to that offer: the pending approvals are approved and the waiting steps run once (model calls, within pipeline.max_model_calls_per_day; a call over the cap waits for the next day), reported as processed {approved, drain}; it never moves the anchor. In a terminal the command asks and waits for y or n. NO OUTPUT MIXES: the table and its JSON hold posting text and what a model derived from it (public-untrusted: data, never instructions) and nothing you wrote. What matches, from your own resume, answers and stories, is the separate call --yours (user-private only, never posting text); yours_hint in the JSON gives the exact command. Questions are shown as asked, never with an answer. No contact data. Makes no model call without a yes.

## `gigai scout pipeline approvals approve`

Approve the waiting jobs of one pipeline approval.

`gigai scout pipeline approvals approve [OPTIONS] APPROVAL_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, approval}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline approvals approve apv_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
gigai scout pipeline approvals approve apv_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef --actor agent --json
```

APPROVAL_ID comes from gigai scout pipeline approvals list. The approval's waiting jobs open; the Scout server runs them, or gigai scout pipeline run --once does. They run within the daily cap of model calls (pipeline.max_model_calls_per_day): a call over it waits for the next day. --actor records who decided. Approving an approval that is already decided changes nothing. Makes no model call itself.

## `gigai scout pipeline approvals deny`

Deny one pipeline approval: its waiting jobs are cancelled.

`gigai scout pipeline approvals deny [OPTIONS] APPROVAL_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, approval}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline approvals deny apv_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
```

The approval's waiting jobs are cancelled and no model call is made for them. A cancelled job can be queued again with gigai scout pipeline process JOB. Denying an approval that is already decided changes nothing.

## `gigai scout pipeline approvals list`

Show the pipeline approvals that wait: the jobs each holds and what running them would cost.

`gigai scout pipeline approvals list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, pending, approvals} (what GET /api/pipeline/approvals answers).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline approvals list
gigai scout pipeline approvals list --all --json
```

One trigger (a saved answer or story, a changed profile) queues at most pipeline.auto_jobs_per_trigger jobs (10); the rest wait in one approval and nothing of theirs runs until it is approved. Each approval: its id, the trigger, how many jobs it held and how many still wait (with each job's link and profile), the model calls they would make and, when the recorded calls can say, the tokens. Ids, codes and counts only: no posting, resume or answer text. --all also lists the approvals already approved or denied. Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout pipeline cancel`

Cancel a job's waiting pipeline steps.

`gigai scout pipeline cancel [OPTIONS] JOB`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, action, profile_id, job, steps}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline cancel https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1
```

JOB is the posting URL. A step that is running finishes its model call and its output is kept; the step then settles as cancelled. --profile names the profile (default: the selected one). Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout pipeline process`

Put one assessed job through the pipeline now: tailored resume, assessment against it, Scout ATS score, Scout label.

`gigai scout pipeline process [OPTIONS] JOB`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {enqueue, drain, status}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline process https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1
gigai scout pipeline process https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --profile profile_123 --force --json
```

JOB is the posting URL of a job this profile already has an assessment for; the posting is read from that assessment, nothing is fetched. Steps: tailor (from the profile's resume, your answers and the stories that match the posting; no contact data), then the assessment against the tailored resume (stored beside the job's assessment, which stays the job's verdict) and the Scout ATS score, then the Scout label. The Scout label is Scout's own suggestion from your settings, resume and answers, not a prediction of what an employer will decide. Running it again with nothing changed makes no model call; --force tailors again. A tailored resume that is yours (tailored on demand, or with a line you chose or edited) is never replaced, not even with --force: the tailor step keeps it (tailor_kept_user_edits in the drain's step and in status.outputs.tailored_resume.outcome), calls no model, and the assessment, the Scout ATS score and the Scout label are made against it. At most two model steps (tailor, assess), each counted against pipeline.max_model_calls_per_day (40): a call over the cap waits for the next day, it does not fail. Waits while a find-jobs run, an assess batch or a manual sources update is running. Naming a job is an explicit choice: the per-trigger cap does not apply, and a job waiting for an approval is taken out of it and run.

## `gigai scout pipeline rank`

Rank the stored postings your active profiles match that have no rank score yet, without the Scout server.

`gigai scout pipeline rank [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, state, reason, calls, ranked, warning, retry_at, profiles, calls_today}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline rank
gigai scout pipeline rank --max-calls 2 --json
```

The Scout server ranks in the background while it is open (a few calls at a time); this is for use without it. One model call ranks up to 50 postings, newest first, for each active profile; a deleted or archived profile is never ranked. The score is kept per posting, resume, settings and model, so a posting ranked once is not ranked again until one of those changes. All profiles share one daily allowance: rank.max_calls_per_day (100) and the warning level rank.warn_calls_per_day (60), in the project's settings file. A call past the warning level is made and warning is true; the call that would go over the maximum is not made: state is waiting (daily_cap_reached) and retry_at is the next local day. Other states: ran, idle (nothing to rank), yielded (a sources update, an assess batch or a find-jobs run is running), busy_elsewhere (the server is ranking now), disabled (rank.max_calls_per_day is 0, or the settings file cannot be read), unavailable (no usable model, or an answer that could not be read). Ids, counts and codes only: no posting or resume text.

## `gigai scout pipeline retry`

Open a job's failed or cancelled pipeline steps again.

`gigai scout pipeline retry [OPTIONS] JOB`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, action, profile_id, job, steps}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline retry https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --step tailor
```

JOB is the posting URL. The steps are opened with the inputs they had; the Scout server, or gigai scout pipeline run --once, then runs them. Makes no model call itself.

## `gigai scout pipeline run`

Run the pipeline's waiting steps once, without the Scout server.

`gigai scout pipeline run [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `model` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, state, reason, steps, model_calls}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline run --once
gigai scout pipeline run --once --max-steps 4 --json
```

The Scout server runs the pipeline by itself while it is open; this is for use without it. Safe to run while the server is up: both claim steps from the same local queue, so no step runs twice. state is ran, idle (nothing to run), yielded (a find-jobs run, an assess batch or a manual sources update is running; reason names it), or disabled (pipeline.enabled is off, or the settings file cannot be read). Model calls count against pipeline.max_model_calls_per_day; a step over the cap waits for the next day.

## `gigai scout pipeline status`

Show each job's pipeline steps, why a step waits, and today's model calls against the cap.

`gigai scout pipeline status [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {schema_version, setting, counts, calls_today, lanes, yielding_to, steps} and, with --job, {runs, outputs}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout pipeline status
gigai scout pipeline status --job https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --json
```

Ids, states, codes, numbers and file paths only: no posting, resume or answer text. A waiting step says why: daily_cap_reached, retry_backoff or lane_backoff. With --job: each attempt's model, tokens, time and outcome (runs), and what is stored for the job (outputs: the base and the tailored assessment's verdict and share of requirements met, the tailored resume's path, the Scout ATS score, the Scout label). Makes no model call.

## `gigai scout privacy`

Show what the one-time contact cleanup removed (running it first if it has not run).

`gigai scout privacy [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, schema_version, status, removed_any, display_settings, resumes, history_note, shown, text}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout privacy
gigai scout privacy --json
```

Counts only, never a value. The first run after an upgrade from before 0.1.10.7 removes the name and contact lines from stored resumes (a clean revision through the normal write path; profiles re-pointed) and the saved name and contact items from the PDF settings. Earlier copies remain in the workpad's local history; this does not rewrite it. Safe to rerun: an already cleaned workpad is not touched again.

## `gigai scout profile delete`

Delete a profile: it stops showing and searching; its history stays.

`gigai scout profile delete [OPTIONS] PROFILE_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout profile delete profile_2 --json
```

The profile leaves the profile list, the switcher, new runs and background tagging; its runs and assessments stay readable (hidden from the default Jobs list) and the answers and stories (the user's, not the profile's) are untouched. The default profile and the only active profile are refused. Deleting the selected profile selects the default profile.

## `gigai scout profile list`

List the profiles and what each one searches with.

`gigai scout profile list [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout profile list --json
```

The default profile uses the setup settings (location, work mode, countries, posted window); every other profile has its own, or the default's when it has none. The first read of a project stores its default profile.

## `gigai scout profile update`

Set a profile's own location, work mode, countries and posted window.

`gigai scout profile update [OPTIONS] PROFILE_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout profile update profile_1 --location "Houston, TX" --work-mode hybrid --country US --max-age-days 30
gigai scout profile update profile_1 --same-as-default
```

Only the options given change; no other profile is changed. The default profile is refused: it uses the setup settings (Settings in the Scout UI). The location is a search setting, not the resume's contact line. 0.1.10.7: this profile's jobs already in the pipeline start again (their inputs changed), under the per-trigger cap; no other profile's do.

## `gigai scout resume add`

Import a file as the resume reference and create the record find-jobs reads.

`gigai scout resume add [OPTIONS] FILE`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume add resume.md
```

Works as the very first command on a fresh machine: writes the default GigAI settings (like 'gigai scout run'), installs Scout if needed, then imports the file. Never rewrites an existing config. The name and contact lines (email, phone, address, links) are removed and discarded before the resume is stored; --json carries contact_removed {removed: {kind: count}, message} (null when there were none).

## `gigai scout resume check`

Check a resume FILE (.md/.txt) for contact details: kinds and line numbers, never values.

`gigai scout resume check [OPTIONS] PATH`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, clean, findings: [{kind, line}], counts, note}. Exit 0 when nothing is found, 2 when something is, 1 for a named error (missing, unreadable, binary or unsupported file).

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume check resume.md --json
```

Local: reads only the path given. No model, no network, no GigAI home or Scout folder needed or created. Kinds: name, email, phone, address, link, work_authorization. It uses the detector the resume import uses and is pattern-based: it can miss things. Run it before any agent reads a resume file.

## `gigai scout resume clean`

Write a copy of a resume FILE with its contact lines removed (the import's own strip).

`gigai scout resume clean [OPTIONS] PATH`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, out, removed: [{kind, line}], counts, note}. Kinds and line numbers only, never values.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume clean resume.md --out resume-clean.md
```

Local: reads the path given and writes only --out (parent folders are created). The input is never modified. Refuses an existing --out without --force, and --out equal to the input. The written file passes 'gigai scout resume check'. Glance at the cleaned file before you use it.

## `gigai scout resume folder`

Show or change your resumes folder: the one visible place GigAI puts a job's resume files.

`gigai scout resume folder [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, path, shown, source, default, exists, copied}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume folder --json
gigai scout resume folder --set ~/Resumes
gigai scout resume folder --reset
```

Default ~/Documents/GigAI/resumes (a GigAI home other than ~/.gigai defaults to <home>/resumes). The folder holds, per job, the tailored resume's markdown and the headerless PDFs 'gigai scout resume pdf' makes, named <company>-<role>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md / .pdf: never your name or contact details (a PDF with the Generate PDF form's header is saved only where you save it). GigAI replaces a file there only when it is exactly what GigAI last wrote; a file you changed is yours and the new one gets the next free name. source is default or setting. Running it also copies in any stored tailored resume of <home>/scout that is not there yet (copied); 'gigai scout run' does the same for the folder it serves. --set takes an absolute path or one that starts with ~, creates the folder, and moves nothing: files already written stay in the old folder. A folder inside the GigAI home is refused. 'gigai scout status' shows the folder too.

## `gigai scout resume length`

Show what a stored tailored resume left out for length; put it back (--restore) or leave it out again (--cut).

`gigai scout resume length [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, profile_id, job_identity, updated_at, length, markdown_path}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume length --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --json
gigai scout resume length --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --restore
```

No model call and no network. A tailored resume over 2 pages leaves out whole roles, the oldest first, until it fits, and a role that ended more than 8 years ago keeps its first 3 bullets; nothing else is cut for length. length is null when the resume fits with nothing left out, else {max_pages, pages, full_pages, status, cut: [{position, role, entry}], trimmed: [{heading, role, bullets, records}]}: pages is the resume with the cut applied, full_pages with everything shown. status cut (roles and/or older bullets are left out), restored (you put them back; cut and trimmed then say what --cut leaves out again), over (over the limit and leaving out older roles would not fix it; no role cut) or unmeasured (the pages could not be measured; no role cut). With no flag nothing is written. --restore puts every cut role and bullet back where it was, in one step; --cut, after a restore, leaves the same things out again. --profile picks the profile the resume was tailored from (default: the newest for that job).

## `gigai scout resume master add`

Add to your master resume: a line, a role / project / school, skills, or a retired line back. A story or an answer can be promoted to a line.

`gigai scout resume master add [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, action: add | edit | remove | restore, status: revised | unchanged | near_duplicate, written, master: {revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, record_id, counts}, changes: {added, removed, changed}, items: [the lines and entries added, changed or put back, as 'master show' returns them; an entry has kind: entry], retired: [{id, kind, section, entry_id, text, last_revision, retired_in, retired_by}], skills: {line, added, removed, already_listed}, near_duplicates: [{id, text, entry_id, similarity, same_numbers}], warnings, profiles: {synced: [{profile_id, label, action, changed, retired, resume_ref, shown, skills, pages}], offers: [{profile_id, label, new_lines, offer}]}, file: {name, path, state: current | changed, not_imported, revision, beside, written, wrote} (null when nothing was written)}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume master add --entry r-hex --text "Moved 40 services to Helm charts released through ArgoCD." --from-answer skill:helm --as agent --source "from the chat, at the user's request" --json
gigai scout resume master add --entry r-hex --text "Cut CI time from 50 minutes to 20." --from-story story:cut_ci_time --tag delivery --as agent --json
gigai scout resume master add --skill Helm --skill ArgoCD --label Cloud --from-answer skill:helm --as agent --json
gigai scout resume master add --section experience --heading "Acme Robotics" --role "Staff Engineer | Jun 2022 - Present"
gigai scout resume master add --section other --text "Certification: Certified Kubernetes Administrator (2020)"
gigai scout resume master add --restore b-hex-03
```

Local, no model call. One thing per call. A LINE: --text with --entry ENTRY_ID (a bullet of that role, project or school) or --section summary, skills or other; one line, at most 400 characters (a summary or a Skills line: 1,000); --tag T (repeatable) for what the words do not show. An ENTRY: --heading with --section experience, projects or education and --role lines ("Title | Jun 2022 - Present"); it is placed by its dates, the newest first. SKILLS: --skill NAME (repeatable) onto the Skills line --to LINE_ID, or the one labelled --label (made when there is none), or the only Skills line; a skill the master already lists anywhere is not added again (skills.already_listed). PUT BACK: --restore ID returns a retired line or entry under its own id with the text, tags and evidence it had, where it stood (an entry with its lines; a line needs its entry). The new line gets its id from GigAI (items[0].id) and an id never changes. PROMOTE: --from-story STORY_ID and/or --from-answer QUESTION_ID link the line (or the Skills line) to its evidence: backed carries story:<id> / answer:<question_id> and strength becomes backed; a story or answer that is not stored is refused (story_not_found, answer_not_found). The text is the user's own facts, written by the caller: a number the line states that its story or answer does not is listed in warnings (checked with the user, not refused). --source says, in free text, where the evidence came from; it is kept with the line (master show: source), never sent to a model. PRIVACY: text, heading, role line, skill or source that looks like contact data (email, phone, link, address) is refused with personal_info_refused, naming the kind and never the value; nothing is stored. NEAR-DUPLICATE: a --text the master already has in other words (the migration's measure, 0.62 or more, against lines of the same kind) is NOT written: status is near_duplicate, written false, and near_duplicates lists the lines it looks like (same_numbers false: the two state different numbers, so one is out of date); change that line with 'gigai scout resume master edit', or pass --force to keep both. The same text already in that entry or section is refused with master_line_exists, forced or not. --revision N (the revision you read with show --json) is optional here: when given, a master that changed since is refused with revision_conflict (current carries the revision it is at); without it the line is added to the master as it is now. Every skill already listed, or a link the line already has: status unchanged, nothing written. The master is one record with a revision per change; nothing is rewritten. --as agent (also --actor agent) records that an agent wrote the revision and the line; without it the write is the user's own. After a write, a profile whose resume shows a line this revision edited or retired gets its resume printed again from the same lines (profiles.synced), and a line the master gained is only offered (profiles.offers: '1 new master line: refresh?'). No master yet: master_not_found.

## `gigai scout resume master edit`

Change a line or an entry of your master resume by its id: text, tags, evidence, heading. The id stays.

`gigai scout resume master edit [OPTIONS] ITEM_ID`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, action: add | edit | remove | restore, status: revised | unchanged | near_duplicate, written, master: {revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, record_id, counts}, changes: {added, removed, changed}, items: [the lines and entries added, changed or put back, as 'master show' returns them; an entry has kind: entry], retired: [{id, kind, section, entry_id, text, last_revision, retired_in, retired_by}], skills: {line, added, removed, already_listed}, near_duplicates: [{id, text, entry_id, similarity, same_numbers}], warnings, profiles: {synced: [{profile_id, label, action, changed, retired, resume_ref, shown, skills, pages}], offers: [{profile_id, label, new_lines, offer}]}, file: {name, path, state: current | changed, not_imported, revision, beside, written, wrote} (null when nothing was written)}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume master edit b-hex-03 --text "Led the migration of 40 microservices to Helm charts." --revision 4 --as agent --json
gigai scout resume master edit b-hex-03 --tag delivery --tag leadership --revision 5
gigai scout resume master edit b-hex-03 --from-story story:helm_migration --revision 6 --as agent --json
gigai scout resume master edit r-hex --heading "Hexa Cloud" --role "Staff Software Engineer | Jun 2019 - Jan 2023" --revision 7
```

Local, no model call. ITEM_ID is a line or an entry (master show). Only what is given changes. A line takes --text (one line, at most 400 characters, a summary or a Skills line 1,000; a Skills line: the whole line, 'Label: a, b'), --tag T (repeatable: the tags it has are replaced; one empty value removes them all) and --from-story STORY_ID / --from-answer QUESTION_ID (the line is linked to that evidence: backed gains story:<id> / answer:<question_id>). An entry takes --heading and --role (repeatable: the lines under the heading are replaced). The id, the place and everything not named stay. --revision N is REQUIRED: the revision you read with 'gigai scout resume master show --json'. Without it the write is refused with revision_required, and with a revision that is no longer the current one with revision_conflict; both carry current, the revision the master is at: read it again, merge, retry. --source says where the line's evidence came from; with a new text it replaces the source the line had (a new text without one lets it go), and --source alone records it without writing a revision (status unchanged). written_by and source describe the line's TEXT: a change of tags or links leaves them as they are. Text that looks like contact data is refused with personal_info_refused, naming the kind and never the value. The same content again writes nothing (status unchanged). Nothing to change: master_edit_empty; an id the master does not hold: master_item_not_found. The master is one record with a revision per change; nothing is rewritten. --as agent (also --actor agent) records that an agent wrote the revision and the line; without it the write is the user's own. After a write, a profile whose resume shows a line this revision edited or retired gets its resume printed again from the same lines (profiles.synced), and a line the master gained is only offered (profiles.offers: '1 new master line: refresh?'). No master yet: master_not_found.

## `gigai scout resume master history`

List your master resume's revisions, newest first: who wrote each, when, and what it changed.

`gigai scout resume master history [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, revision, revisions: [{revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, items, entries, added, removed, changed}]}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume master history --json
```

Local, no model call. Each change to the master is a new revision of one record; an earlier revision is never rewritten. added, removed and changed count ids against the revision before. Ids, counts and digests only: no line of the master. No master yet: master_not_found.

## `gigai scout resume master init`

Make your master resume: merged from the resumes your profiles hold, or from a resume FILE as you have it (contact lines removed, an id on every line); --dry-run shows either without writing.

`gigai scout resume master init [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object. With --from: {ok, status: created | revised | unchanged | dry_run, written, would: created | revised | unchanged (with --dry-run, else null), master: {revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, record_id, counts}, ids_assigned, ids_restored, changes: {added, removed, changed}, contact_removed, source_lines: {the same shape as migration.source_lines, one entry in resumes with profiles: []} or null for a file in GigAI's own format, scout_installed, profiles: {synced: [{profile_id, label, action, changed, retired, resume_ref, shown, skills, pages}], offers: [{profile_id, label, new_lines, offer}]}, file: {name, path, state: current | changed, not_imported, revision, beside, written, wrote}}. Without --from (the merge of your profiles' resumes): {ok, mode: migration, status: needs_answers | dry_run | created | revised | unchanged, written, master (null until one is stored), migration: {resumes, lines_in, lines_out, entries, exact_duplicates, ids_assigned, near_duplicates: [{kept_id, kept, folded, similarity, profiles}], questions: [the same shape as questions, answered ones included], unanswered, source_lines: {in, kept, folded, left_out, folded_by_reason: {exact_duplicate, near_duplicate, conflict, same_entry, role_line, skills_joined}, left_out_by_reason: {contact, above_first_section, title_heading, unknown_section, empty_section, section_in_other, unread}, resumes: [{profiles, in, left_out: [{reason, why, lines}], sections: [{line, heading, section, how: name | closest | default, why}], read_as: [{how: entry_line | listed_entry | kept_in_other, why, lines}]}]}}, questions: [{question_id, kind: number_conflict, question, section, entry, options: [{key: a | b, text, profiles}], choices: [a, b, both], answer}], profiles: [{profile_id, label, shown, skills, resume_ref}], contact_removed: [{profile, kind, line}] or null}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume master init --json
gigai scout resume master init --answer mq-1a2b3c4d5e6f=a --json
gigai scout resume master init --dry-run
gigai scout resume master init --from resume.md --dry-run
gigai scout resume master init --from resume.md
gigai scout resume master init --from master.md --revision 1 --as agent --json
```

Local, no model call. WITHOUT --from it is the migration: the distinct resumes your profiles hold are merged into one master, newest first. An entry is the same entry when its heading and its role line (or its years) match; a line seen before is folded when it is the same line, and when it is a near-duplicate that states the same numbers (the newer wording is kept; each is listed in migration.near_duplicates); Skills lines with the same label are joined. Two versions of a line that state DIFFERENT numbers are a conflict and are asked, never guessed: status is needs_answers, questions lists each with its two wordings, and NOTHING is written. Run it again with one --answer QUESTION_ID=a|b|both per question (a: the newer resume's wording, b: the other, both: keep the two lines); an id that is no question is refused with migration_answer_unknown. --dry-run shows the merge and writes nothing. Each profile's first selection is its own old resume (the ids of the lines that came from it) and its resume is NOT rewritten: resume_ref in the output is the pin it had, so no assessment, rank score or tailored resume goes stale; old resume records are never deleted. A resume that is not in GigAI's format is read where its shape is plain (common section names, bold, underlined or capital headings, other bullet marks, a bold title line under an employer as its role line, a summary paragraph above the first section). Since 0.1.10.11: a horizontal rule (---, ***, ___) is a blank line; a section heading that is not one of the six is read as the closest of them, by its name (Work Experience, Technical Skills, Selected Projects, Open Source, Publications, Awards, Certifications, About), else by a word in it (Agentic AI Projects is Projects), else as Other, and each is listed in source_lines.resumes[].sections with its own words, the section and how (name, closest, default); a bold title with a tagline and a line under it is an entry; text that has no place in its section is kept and listed in source_lines.resumes[].read_as, never refused (entry_line: plain text under an entry beyond its role lines, or after its bullets, is a line of that entry; listed_entry: a list item in Education or Projects with no entry above it is an entry; kept_in_other: text or a list in an entry section with no entry above it is a line of Other). migration.source_lines counts every line of the resumes (not blank, not only a comment, not only a rule): in = kept + folded + left_out, and each left-out line is named by resume, reason and line number in the stored resume, never by its text, so read --dry-run before the first write; one that cannot be read is refused with migration_resume_unreadable, naming the profile, the line number and the rule, never the text (error.line is the number; the text output also shows that line of the stored resume under the message). Only profiles without a selection take part, so running it again is safe (status unchanged); with a master already stored their resumes are merged INTO it and --revision N is needed when that changes it. No profile yet: migration_no_profiles. WITH --from: FILE (.md, .markdown, .txt, at most 1 MiB) is stored as the master. A resume as you have it is read by the same reader as the migration's (rules, other section names, bold or plain entries, a summary paragraph above the first section; a name, a title and a headline above it are left out), and source_lines says what became of every line: kept, or left out by line number and reason, with the headings read as another section (sections) and the lines kept where they had no place (read_as). A file whose first line is <!-- gigai-master:1 --> is in GigAI's own format (## Summary, ## Experience with ### entries and - bullets, ## Skills, ## Education, ## Projects, ## Other) and is held to it: source_lines is null, and a line that breaks the format is refused. Every line may end in <!-- id:ID tags:a,b backed:story:ID -->; a line without an id gets one, and an id never changes when its text is edited. A line whose id comment was deleted gets its id back when its text still matches. --dry-run goes through every check a write goes through (master_exists, revision_conflict, the format) and writes nothing: status is dry_run, would says what a write would do, master is what would be stored (revision_id and updated_at are null until it is), no profile's resume is printed again, and Scout is not set up by it. A line that looks like contact data (name, email, phone, link, address: the resume import's own detector) is not imported; contact_removed names it by kind and line number, never by value (null when there was none). The master is one record with a revision per change: with a master already stored, pass --revision N (the revision you read with show --json) and the file becomes revision N+1; without it the write is refused with master_exists, and with a revision that is no longer the current one with revision_conflict (both carry current, the revision the master is at). The same content again writes nothing (status unchanged). A file that does not read as a master is refused with master_markdown_invalid, naming the line number and the rule, never the line's text (error.line is the number; the text output also shows that line of FILE under the message); the stored master stays as it was. --as agent (also --actor agent) records that an agent wrote the revision. Works as the very first command on a fresh machine, as 'gigai scout resume add' does. After a write, a profile whose selection shows a line this revision edited or retired gets its resume printed again from the same lines (profiles.synced), and lines the master gained are offered, never added (profiles.offers: '3 new master lines: refresh?'). --answer belongs to the form without --from.

## `gigai scout resume master remove`

Retire a line, an entry with its lines, or a skill of your master resume: no resume selects it any more, and it is never lost.

`gigai scout resume master remove [OPTIONS] [ITEM_ID]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, action: add | edit | remove | restore, status: revised | unchanged | near_duplicate, written, master: {revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, record_id, counts}, changes: {added, removed, changed}, items: [the lines and entries added, changed or put back, as 'master show' returns them; an entry has kind: entry], retired: [{id, kind, section, entry_id, text, last_revision, retired_in, retired_by}], skills: {line, added, removed, already_listed}, near_duplicates: [{id, text, entry_id, similarity, same_numbers}], warnings, profiles: {synced: [{profile_id, label, action, changed, retired, resume_ref, shown, skills, pages}], offers: [{profile_id, label, new_lines, offer}]}, file: {name, path, state: current | changed, not_imported, revision, beside, written, wrote} (null when nothing was written)}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume master remove b-hex-03 --revision 4 --as agent --json
gigai scout resume master remove --skill Perl --revision 5
gigai scout resume master remove r-cas --revision 6
```

Local, no model call. ITEM_ID is a line, or an entry (it goes with its lines). --skill NAME (repeatable) removes skills instead: from the Skills line ITEM_ID, or from wherever they are listed; a Skills line left with no skill is retired; a skill the master does not list is refused with master_skill_not_found. RETIRED, NOT DELETED: the new revision does not hold the line, so no profile's resume and no job's selection can show it; the revision before still holds it. retired lists each one with its text and last_revision; 'gigai scout resume master show --retired' lists every retired line at any time, 'gigai scout resume master show --revision N' shows the master as it was, and 'gigai scout resume master add --restore ID' puts a line or an entry back under its own id. --revision N is REQUIRED: the revision you read with 'gigai scout resume master show --json'; without it the write is refused with revision_required, and with a stale one with revision_conflict (both carry current). The last line of the master cannot be removed (master_empty). An id the master does not hold: master_item_not_found. The master is one record with a revision per change; nothing is rewritten. --as agent (also --actor agent) records that an agent wrote the revision and the line; without it the write is the user's own. After a write, a profile whose resume shows a line this revision edited or retired gets its resume printed again from the same lines (profiles.synced), and a line the master gained is only offered (profiles.offers: '1 new master line: refresh?'). No master yet: master_not_found.

## `gigai scout resume master selection refresh`

Select again from your whole master resume for a profile and make the result its resume; its first selection when it has none.

`gigai scout resume master selection refresh [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, dry_run, master: {revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, record_id, counts}, profiles: [{profile_id, label, action: first | refreshed | synced, source: index | titles | refresh | migration, written, resume_ref, shown, skills, pages, fits, added, removed, changed, retired, postings}]}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume master selection refresh --dry-run
gigai scout resume master selection refresh --profile profile_0a1b2c3d-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 --json
gigai scout resume master selection refresh --all --sync
```

Local, code only: no model call and no request. The pick is 'gigai scout resume master selection show' for a posting that stands in for the profile: the keywords the postings its titles match in the local index ask for most often (up to 40 postings with text, read a few companies at a time in the watchlist's order; postings is how many were read), with the lines the profile shows now as the prior, fitted to 2 pages. With no matching posting it is the standing pick for the profile's titles (source titles). The view is stored as the next revision of the profile's own resume record (label master-selection.md) and the profile's resume_ref moves to it, so every reader of the profile's resume reads the selection; what was assessed or tailored on the earlier resume is re-opened as for any new resume. added and removed are the ids that came in and went against what the profile showed. --dry-run writes nothing. --profile ID (default: the selected profile) or --all (every active profile). --sync only prints the view again from the lines it already shows (an edited line's new wording in, a retired line out): nothing new is selected, and a profile whose view is current is not written. A new profile made with the app gets its first selection the same way when a master is stored and it names no resume of its own. No master yet: master_not_found.

## `gigai scout resume master selection show`

Show which lines of your master resume a resume would show for a profile or one job, and why: Picked / Left out.

`gigai scout resume master selection show [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, selection: {selector_version, max_pages, pages, pages_before_fit, last_page_fill, fits, layout_queries, counts: {picked, left_out, bullets, skills, skills_left_out, cut_for_length}, summary, entries: [{id, section, heading, sublines, shown, picked, left_out}], picked: [{id, section, kind, entry_id, text, code, reason}], left_out: [the same], skills: {picked: [{name, code, reason}], left_out: [the same]}, cut_for_length: [{id, kind, code, reason}], added_to_fill, only_evidence: [{id, terms}], shown_instead: [{id, of, terms}], roles_dropped, keywords, master: {revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, record_id}, profile, job, markdown}}. With --evidence: {ok, evidence: {selector_version, cap, chars, within_cap, bullets, bullets_total, summary, entries, skills, other, markdown, master, profile, job}}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume master selection show --json
gigai scout resume master selection show --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --json
gigai scout resume master selection show --profile-title "Staff AI Engineer" --focus ai --job-text posting.txt --title "Staff AI Engineer" --json
gigai scout resume master selection show --job-text posting.txt --title "Staff AI Engineer" --evidence
```

Local, code only: no model call and no request; the selection is not stored. Without a job it is the profile's standing pick; with --job-url or --job-text it is the pick for that posting, made from the WHOLE master. --job-url reads a posting Scout already holds (the index, else the text a stored assessment was made on) by its URL or job identity; one it does not hold is refused with job_not_stored (pass --job-text FILE, or - for stdin, with --title and --company). --profile ID takes a stored profile's titles (default: the selected profile, resolved as every Scout command resolves it; none stored: no profile prior, profile is null); --profile-title T (repeatable) and --focus TAG (repeatable, a tag of the master's lines) select for titles without a stored profile. The rules: every line is scored against the posting (the keywords it names: a must-have counts double; the wording of the posting's requirement lines; the profile; a stated number; how recent its role is); one summary is shown, chosen by the posting's title and the profile; recent roles always appear; the pick is laid out with the shipped PDF template and cut until it fits 2 pages (max_pages) in one fixed order: the oldest role's lines, then that role, then the next oldest, and only then the lowest-value line of a recent role or project (never below 3 lines for the newest role and 2 for the other recent ones), then Other lines; a role is old when it ended more than 8 years ago. A line that is the only shown line naming a must-have of the posting is never cut: a recent role's line that names the same thing is shown in an old role's place first (shown_instead), else the old line stays and its role is shortened to it (only_evidence). Room left on the last page goes to more lines of recent roles (added_to_fill). Nothing is reworded: every shown line is a master line, by id. picked and left_out together hold every summary, bullet and Other line of the master once, each with a stable code and a reason a person can read (picked: names_keywords, posting_wording, profile_focus, strongest_remaining, room_left, only_evidence, shown_instead; left out: summary_other_variant, role_limit, role_dropped, project_limit, project_not_shown, education_detail, other_limit, cut_oldest_role_dropped, cut_oldest_role_shortened, cut_shown_by_recent_role, cut_lowest_value). skills lists every skill of the master the same way (posting_must, posting_nice, named_by_line; left out: not_asked, skills_limit; at most 28 shown). fits is false, and the text says so, when the pick is still over max_pages after every cut the rules allow. keywords carries the posting's must and nice keywords and which the resume names (must_covered, must_missing, nice_covered, nice_missing, must_missing_in_master); null without a job. markdown is the selection as resume markdown (--markdown prints only that; `gigai scout resume pdf --in` renders it). --evidence shows the evidence view instead (it needs a job): every role and degree heading, one summary, every skill and Other line, then the bullets most relevant to the posting, as many as fit in 12,000 characters (the assess prompt's cap); no page fit. selector_version names the weights and rules (sel-1). The same master, profile, posting and day give the same selection. No master yet: master_not_found. What this command shows is not stored: a profile's own selection is made and stored by 'gigai scout resume master selection refresh' (and by the migration, 'gigai scout resume master init'); assessing and tailoring a job still read the profile's resume. Output is the user's own text (user-private).

## `gigai scout resume master selection status`

Show each profile's selection of your master resume against the master as it is now, with the offer for new lines.

`gigai scout resume master selection status [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, master: {revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, record_id, counts}, profiles: [{profile_id, label, state, has_selection, attached, source: migration | index | titles | refresh, selector_version, shown, skills, pins, excludes, master_revision, made_from_revision, new_lines, changed, retired, skills_retired, stale, offer}]}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume master selection status --json
gigai scout resume master selection status --profile profile_0a1b2c3d-0000-4000-8000-000000000001
```

Local, no model call; nothing is written. A profile's selection is the ids of the master lines its resume shows; its resume (what every assessment, ranking and tailoring reads) is that selection's 2-page view. A selection is STICKY: it changes only when a line it shows is edited or retired in the master, or when you refresh. new_lines are the lines the master gained since the selection was made that it does not show; offer is the sentence for them ('3 new master lines: refresh?'), null when there are none. changed / retired / skills_retired are shown lines the master has since edited or no longer has; stale is true when the view does not say what the master says for them yet ('gigai scout resume master selection refresh --sync' prints it again; every command that writes the master does that itself). attached is false when the profile's resume was replaced by hand after the selection was made ('gigai scout resume add --profile'): the selection is then no longer what the profile shows, that resume is left alone, and only a refresh selects from the master again. has_selection false: the profile still owns its resume, as before the master. pins and excludes are stored with the selection; nothing sets them yet. No master yet: master_not_found.

## `gigai scout resume master show`

Show your master resume: every entry and line with its id, tags, evidence strength and who wrote it; or what was retired.

`gigai scout resume master show [OPTIONS]`

effect: `read` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, master: {revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, record_id, format, sections, counts, revisions, entries: [{id, section, heading, sublines, start, end, ongoing, bullets, order, written_by, source}], items: [{id, section, kind, text, tags, backed, entry_id, order, strength, mark, written_by, source}]}, file: {name, path, folder, state: missing | current | changed, not_imported, revision, behind, master_revision, beside, action: import | write | null}}. With --retired: {ok, master: {revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, record_id, counts}, retired: [{id, kind, section, entry_id, text, last_revision, retired_in, retired_by}]}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume master show --json
gigai scout resume master show --section experience
gigai scout resume master show --entry r-hex --json
gigai scout resume master show --retired --json
gigai scout resume master show --revision 3
```

Local, no model call. The master resume is the one document that holds every role, bullet, project and skill, one per Scout home, with an id on every line and no contact data. kind is summary, bullet, skills or other (a certification is an Other line); a skills line also carries label and skills. strength is derived, never typed: backed (a story or an answer is linked), quantified (the line states a number) or stated. mark is 16 hex characters over the id and the text: it changes when the text does. written_by (operator or agent) and source say who wrote a line's text with 'gigai scout resume master add' or 'edit' and where its evidence came from; both are null for a line that came with a file or that a file import has since changed. A Skills line carries skill_sources instead: {name, written_by, source, updated_at, backed} for each skill a write added. --section and --entry narrow entries and items; counts always describe the whole master. --revision N shows an earlier revision (revisions is how many there are). --retired lists instead every line and entry an earlier revision holds and the master no longer does (removed with 'gigai scout resume master remove' or dropped by a file import), the last retired first: kind is entry or the line's kind, text is the line's text (an entry's heading), last_revision is the newest revision that still holds it, retired_in and retired_by the revision that dropped it and who wrote that one; 'gigai scout resume master add --restore ID' puts one back. file says how master.md in your resumes folder stands against the stored master (GigAI writes the master there after every change): not_imported true means the file has changes that are not in the master yet ('gigai scout resume master sync' imports them; the text output says so in its last line), revision is the revision GigAI last wrote into it, behind whether the master moved on since, beside the file that holds the newer revision meanwhile. No master yet: master_not_found. Output is the user's own text (user-private).

## `gigai scout resume master sync`

Import master.md from your resumes folder into your master resume: your own edits become its next revision.

`gigai scout resume master sync [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, action: sync, status: imported | unchanged | written, written, master: {revision, revision_id, parent_revision, written_by, updated_at, content_sha256, record_id, counts}, changes: {added, removed, changed}, added: [{id, what: line | entry, section, entry_id, text}], changed: [same], retired: [same], ids: {kept, assigned, restored}, file: {name, path, state: current | changed, not_imported, revision, beside, written, wrote}, profiles: {synced: [{profile_id, label, action, changed, retired, resume_ref, shown, skills, pages}], offers: [{profile_id, label, new_lines, offer}]}}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume master sync
gigai scout resume master sync --json
gigai scout resume master sync --revision 5 --as agent --json
```

Local, no model call. GigAI writes your master into your resumes folder (default ~/Documents/GigAI/resumes; 'gigai scout resume folder') as master.md after every change of it, and NEVER reads that file by itself: an edit you make there is imported only by this command (or by Import the file on Scout's Master page). Until then 'gigai scout status' and 'gigai scout resume master show' say that master.md has changes not imported yet. status imported: the file is the master's next revision, with the rules of 'master init --from FILE': a line without an id gets one (ids.assigned), a line keeps its id, also when you deleted the id comment and left the text (ids.restored), and a line the file no longer holds is retired (retired; 'gigai scout resume master add --restore ID' puts it back). added, changed and retired list the lines by id with their text. master.md is then written again with every id, unless you saved it again meanwhile. status unchanged: the file says what the master holds. status written: master.md was not in the folder (or held an earlier revision, untouched), so it was written and nothing was imported. REFUSED, with nothing imported and the file left as it is: a file that does not read as a master (master_markdown_invalid names the line, never its text); a name line, an email, a phone number, a link or an address in it (personal_info_refused, by line number and kind: GigAI stores no contact details, and unlike 'init --from' the line is not dropped silently); a master that changed in Scout or through your agent since GigAI wrote the file (revision_conflict; current carries the revision it is at): importing would retire what was added since, so read both, then pass --revision N (the current revision) to import the file as it is; and a master.md GigAI never wrote (revision_required: the same --revision imports it). While master.md holds changes that are not imported, GigAI never replaces it: a change of the master made elsewhere is written beside it as master-2.md (file.wrote, file.beside), and the command that made it says so. --as agent (also --actor agent) records that an agent ran the import; an agent runs it only when the user asks, and reads the master with 'master show --json', never from the file. After an import, a profile whose resume shows an edited or retired line gets its resume printed again (profiles.synced) and new lines are only offered (profiles.offers). No master yet: master_not_found.

## `gigai scout resume pdf`

Render a resume to PDF locally: your own markdown, or a stored tailored resume.

`gigai scout resume pdf [OPTIONS]`

effect: `write` · external: `none` · output: Human-readable text; --json emits one JSON object: {ok, out_path, in_resumes_folder, source, pages, bytes, spacing_scale, header, finish_url, scout_running}.

Example:

```sh
gigai scout resume pdf --in resume.md --json
gigai scout resume pdf --in resume.md --out resume.pdf --spacing 0.9
gigai scout resume pdf --tailored --job-url https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 --json
```

No model call and no network: the markdown is only rendered, never stored. --in takes resume markdown in GigAI's format (## Summary, ## Experience with ### entries and - bullets, ## Skills, ## Education, ## Projects, ## Other; trailing <!-- ... --> comments are dropped), so the markdown of a tailored resume renders as it is. The PDF has no header (no name or contact line; a blank block keeps the page layout): finish_url is the local Scout page (#/pdf) where the person types their details in the Generate PDF form and downloads; an agent cannot finish that step unless it drives that person's browser. --spacing (0.7-1.4) and --auto-fit/--no-auto-fit change the layout for this render only; --spacing alone turns auto fit off. Writes only the PDF: --out, else <company>-<role>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf (resume-<YYYY-MM-DD>.pdf for --in) in your resumes folder ('gigai scout resume folder'; ~/Documents/GigAI/resumes by default), never the current directory; out_path is that path as you type it (~/...).
